# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I cannot yet distinguish any wire, marking, display, or light by touch. I should avoid cutting until the Mute reports the manual and the Deaf reports the bomb’s visible information. No safe gesture protocol has been established, so I will not send an ambiguous signal.

``` 
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Visible state: display is 0. Indicator light is red. Wires from 1 to 3 are blue, green, red. Mute signalled six gestures in this order: first repeated twice, second repeated twice, third, fourth.

The Deaf has provided the tactilely relevant colour order: wire 1 blue, wire 2 green, wire 3 red. However, the manual’s six-gesture message is not yet meaningful to me because I cannot see gestures, and no gesture code has been established. I will ask the Mute to have the Deaf identify the actual gesture symbols, so the manual information can be relayed in words.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please signal to Deaf that Deaf should report the exact identity or ordinary description of each of your six gestures to Blind.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display remains 0; wires remain 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red; indicator light is now white. Mute signalled three repetitions of the first gesture.

The wire colours and light have changed only in the Deaf’s report; I still have no manual rule. The gesture repetitions remain uninterpretable to me, so cutting any wire would be a guess. I will ask Mute to use the Deaf as a reporting channel, explicitly requesting descriptions of the gesture symbols rather than another repetition pattern.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot see your gestures. Have Deaf describe aloud to Blind the exact symbol or ordinary hand-shape of every gesture you signal, in order. Do not merely repeat them.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current state: display 0; light is green; wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red. Mute gestures were: ? ? ? ? ? ? ? — three upward index signs, two V signs, crossed fingers, then raised palm.

The Deaf has now identified the gesture sequence as three upward-index signs, two V signs, crossed fingers, and a raised palm, but that is still only a signal pattern—not the manual’s meaning. Since the Mute can hear me and read the manual, I should request the rule directly in words. The current physical state remains display 0, green light, and wires blue/green/red; cutting remains unsafe without the rule.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please tell me the manual's exact rule in spoken words, including which wire position to cut for display 0, green light, and wires blue, green, red.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current state: display 0; light is red; wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red. Mute signalled exactly: ? ?.

The latest two gestures are still unidentified, and the current light is red. I will establish a simple code that does not depend on knowing gesture names: the Mute should repeat one unmistakable gesture exactly as many times as the wire position required by the manual. The Deaf can count and report that number.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Use one same unmistakable gesture repeated exactly 1, 2, or 3 times to indicate the required wire position for the current state: display 0, red light, wires blue green red. Do not send any other gestures.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Turn 5 state: display 0; light is white; wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red. Mute signalled exactly three upward-pointing gestures: ? ? ?.

The agreed channel was a count of one repeated gesture: one, two, or three repetitions means wire position 1, 2, or 3. Deaf reports exactly three upward-pointing gestures, so the Mute’s answer is wire 3. The latest reported state is display 0, white light, and wires blue, green, red; I will cut position 3.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=3)
```
